samples.body: A thank you, and a small confession. On Saturday a gentleman brought in four boxes of his late wife's poetry books, and I'm afraid I sat down on the stool behind the counter and read for longer than I should have. She had written the date she bought each one inside the cover, in very tidy pencil, going back to 1961. He said she would have hated them sitting in the loft, and that he'd rather they went to people who would actually open them. So they are on the shelf by the window now, and I have left her pencilled dates exactly where they are. If you buy one, you are buying a little piece of somebody's life, and I think that is rather lovely. Thank you to him, and to everyone who trusts us with the books that mattered to them. Jean

samples.body: We are looking for one or two more volunteers for Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons. I won't pretend it's glamorous. There is a good deal of dusting, a certain amount of carrying, and the till has a temper of its own. But you will meet the nicest people in Norwich, you will learn far more about Victorian railway timetables than you ever expected to, and you will be doing something real for the hospice. When I retired from bookkeeping I assumed I'd had enough of columns of figures for one lifetime. It turns out I quite like counting the day's takings when I know where the money is going. If you can spare three hours a week, do pop in and ask for Moira or me. No experience needed, only patience and a reasonable tolerance for dust.

Took the tree down at the shop this morning. It always feels like the end of something, folding up the lights and unhooking all those little tags. We keep every one of them, bundled up with string, and they go back to the hospice for safekeeping. Ray's was near the top this year, next to one that just said 'Nan, still making us laugh'. I've no idea whose nan she was but I found myself smiling at it all the way home on the bus. The driver must have thought I'd been at the sherry, and on reflection I'm not sure I mind what he thought. Happy new year to everyone who has been kind to me this winter. There have been a lot of you.
